extracted.intended_audience: librarians, information scientists, library planners, and editors of information services
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and desiderata for creating an 'Informatorium'—an ideal information library providing timely scientific indexing, retrieval, publications, and experimental information services. Focus is on services, formats, staffing, cooperation, and technologies needed to meet researchers' information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide variety of information and services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Informatorium will have a wide variety of information covering many subjects and will make announcements and discuss new experimental projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multiple kinds of materials (indexes, abstracts, directories, announcements of projects) so the facility supplies information across a broad subject range rather than being narrowly specialized. Example phrases from text: 'The Informatorium will have a wide variety information ... cover ... scientific ... make announce- and discuss new experimental projects.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid (near-instantaneous) supply/retrieval of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to supply information instantaneously or nearly so to satisfy users' immediate intellectual needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design retrieval systems and workflows so that needed information can be obtained quickly—supporting users 'simultaneously' and meeting 'thirsting' populations. Emphasizes real-time/current-awareness capability rather than slow paper-only delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly trained staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must be highly trained to operate an Informatorium and to select, compile, and disseminate information effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in staff expertise for indexing, abstracting, editorial judgment, format experimentation, and user services. The essay repeatedly notes 'highly trained' staff as integral to the ideal library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive indexing (including citation indexes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multiple indexing services, including citation indexes, subject indexes, and cumulative indexes (e.g., Current Contents cumulated index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain both current-awareness (short-term, cumulated) and retrospective indexing. Support citation indexing as a key retrieval tool. The text cites 'Current Contents ... cumulated index ... citation indexes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracting and selective indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce abstracts and selective indexes to guide readers to relevant literature without requiring them to read everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include selective abstracting services and selective indexing to distill large literatures into manageable, relevant pointers for users ('abstracts, indexes, citation indexes, selective various').

rubrics_metrics.name: Current-awareness publications/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide timely current-awareness products (e.g., Current Contents) that accumulate recent literature in accessible forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer frequent, cumulative publications or services so readers can follow new literature as it appears; maintain short turnaround and consider formats that reduce lag ('Current Contents ... cumulated index months').

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentation with formats and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously experiment with and adopt new formats (layout, paper, two-column, lighter weight) to improve readability, cost, and usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run format experiments (different column widths, lighter paper, different arrangements) and be willing to change layout based on reader feedback and usability. The essay references trials of 'two column', 'new paper', 'lighter', and 'new formats for this directory.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial discipline for publications (deadlines and self-restraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain editorial control, impose deadlines, and exercise self-restraint to produce focused, timely publications in a series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing a series of reports or publications, enforce deadlines and limit scope/length to ensure regular, useful output. Phrases: 'deadline', 'self-restraint', 'staff members', 'a publication ... series'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directories and address information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide directories (author/organization addresses) and up-to-date contact information to assist users in following up on leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include readable, well-arranged directories as part of the information offering; consider arrangement and presentation to make addresses easy to use ('directory ... the address ... to prepare').

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and dissemination using storage technologies (microform, copies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use storage and reproduction technologies (microform, copying) to preserve materials and enable wider dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt microform and other preservation formats to store and distribute documents efficiently; plan for durable, retrievable storage. Text mentions 'microform', 'storage', 'copy-'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation and coordination across institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage cooperation among libraries and information services to share resources, standards, and efforts (e.g., World Brain/Memex ideas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote inter-institutional cooperation for compilation, indexing, and dissemination so efforts are complementary rather than duplicative. The essay references broad cooperative visions and system-level thinking ('cooperation', 'World Brain, Memex').

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of nomenclature and specialized linguistic tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Support specialized tools such as nomenclature services and chemico-linguistics to handle domain-specific retrieval needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop domain-specific vocabularies, nomenclatures, and linguistic aids to improve indexing and retrieval for technical fields ('nomenclature', 'chemico-Linguistics').

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce and discuss new experimental projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Informatorium to publicize and critique new experimental projects and services in information science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sections or channels that report on experiments and innovations so the community can learn and adopt successful approaches ('make announcements and discuss new experimental projects').

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation to reader needs and solicitation of feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit reader suggestions and adapt content, formats, and arrangements in response to user feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act on reader input to improve clarity, arrangement, and usefulness; the author notes reader correspondence and format changes driven by feedback ('from our readers', 'suggestions').

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific orientation and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the Informatorium to satisfy scientific requirements and to be scientifically rigorous in selection and presentation of material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that selection policies, indexing, and summaries meet scientific standards and address researchers' needs for reliable, accurate information ('facility ... to satisfy requir- that will be scientifically').
